tasks.short: Monitor trails, slopes and swimming areas, then patrol them.

steps.what: Monitor trails, slopes and swimming areas from the post.
Patrol those areas on foot or in a vehicle.

tasks.design: The lifeguard monitors trails, slopes and swimming areas from the post, then patrols those areas on foot or in a vehicle. She watches the people who are there. The design adds no camera score and raises no alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hazard is in front of her and changes by the second.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new sees the water, the trail or the slope for her.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to watch and move for the whole shift.
tasks.human_edge: She sees who is in trouble and which post to take next.
tasks.altitude: The week is still watching and walking. No decision right moves.

reach.task: Watch the crossing for the whole shift
reach.learn: A conditions log does not replace watching the people who are there now.

evidence.claim: Watching a pool, beach or slope and moving between posts is physical judgement. A screen of past incidents does not see who is in trouble now. No measured patrol result is used as this operator's saving.

assumptions: Both steps stay at full time because nothing watches or walks for her. No system is added, so upkeep is zero. No alert is raised.

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step changes. She still monitors and patrols for the full time. Upkeep is zero because no system is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Contact emergency medical personnel for a serious injury.

steps.what: Judge whether the injury needs emergency medical personnel.
Contact those personnel and report the injury.

tasks.design: The lifeguard judges whether the injury needs emergency medical personnel, then contacts them herself and reports the place and the injury. The design does not place that call for her.
tasks.previous_blocker: Only the person on the scene knows the injury and the exact place.
tasks.enabler_now: A phone already reaches emergency medical personnel. Nothing new can judge the injury.
tasks.still_hard: She must judge the injury and place the call.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the call is needed and says what she sees.
tasks.altitude: She still decides the call and places it. Nothing changes.

reach.task: Call for medical backup from a scene
reach.learn: The person who sees the injury still places the call.

evidence.claim: Deciding that an injury is serious and calling emergency medical personnel is the lifeguard's act. A form cannot place that call. No measured dispatch result is used as this operator's saving.

assumptions: Both steps stay at full time. She places the call. No message is sent for her, so upkeep is zero.

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step changes. She still judges the injury and places the call for the full time. Upkeep is zero because no system is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Warn participants about weather, unsafe areas or illegal conduct.

steps.what: Notice unsafe weather, areas or illegal conduct.
Warn the participants about that weather or conduct.

tasks.design: The lifeguard notices unsafe weather, unsafe areas or illegal conduct, then warns the participants in person. She speaks the warning herself. No broadcast is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The guest is there and the hazard is local.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new speaks the warning for her.
tasks.still_hard: She must judge the moment and the words.
tasks.human_edge: She matches the warning to the person and the place.
tasks.altitude: She still warns people herself. Nothing changes.

reach.task: Warn a visitor about a closed area
reach.learn: The warning is spoken to the person. A sign does not finish it.

evidence.claim: Warning a guest about weather, an unsafe area or illegal conduct is spoken on the spot. A posted rule does not replace that warning. No measured warning result is used as this operator's saving.

assumptions: Both steps stay at full time. She speaks the warning. No broadcast is added, so upkeep is zero.

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step changes. She still notices the hazard and warns people for the full time. Upkeep is zero because no system is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record weather, beach conditions, treatments and incident information.

steps.what: Note beach conditions the weather station does not show.
Fill the conditions sheet from weather station readings.
Write the treatments and the incident into the records.
Check weather conditions and treatments against what she saw.
Confirm the day's conditions and incident records.
File the confirmed records in the incident log.

tasks.design: The lifeguard notes beach conditions the weather station cannot see and writes each treatment and incident herself. The {OTHER} weather station fills the conditions sheet from its readings, and a separate step files that sheet in the {OTHER} incident log only after she checks it against what she saw and confirms the day. Nothing is posted to the {ERP} and no weather alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition readings and treatment notes lived on paper and were copied into the day log.
tasks.enabler_now: A records form can map station fields and file a confirmed snapshot. The station feed is a contract, not a new kind of judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Treatment words and the check against the real beach or slope stay hers. A missing station feed puts the figures back on her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows whether the reading matches the water or the slope, and what care she gave.
tasks.altitude: She still writes treatments and checks the sheet against what she saw. She no longer copies station figures, and she no longer recopies a confirmed day into the log.

reach.learn: File only the version the person on the scene confirmed, and keep treatment words as that person wrote them.

evidence.claim: Copying a weather-station reading onto a conditions sheet is clerical. Writing the treatment and judging that the reading matches the beach stay with the lifeguard. No measured beach-log result is used as this operator's saving.

AI Act article 5 bans building face databases by untargeted scraping, emotion recognition at work, and crime prediction based only on profiling. This conditions sheet and this incident log do none of those.
GDPR article 9 treats biometric data used to identify a person as special category data. This log does not identify people from biometrics. Treatment notes stay text the lifeguard wrote.

assumptions: Visual condition notes come from s1: hazards, crowd, visibility, closures, and the flag she set.

The weather-station contract is station id, reading time, wind speed, air temperature and water temperature. The station produces those readings. Station runtime is not her time and is not counted as saving. If the feed is missing, s2 does not run and she types those figures inside s1, which stays full time.
Treatment and incident notes come from s3: person, care given, time and place. She writes them. No model drafts the care.
s4 accepts a station line only when it matches the beach or slope she saw, and a treatment line only when the person, the care and the time are present.
s5 confirms the day before s6 files that confirmed version. A later change needs a new confirmation.
Today she copies station figures onto the sheet and then copies the confirmed day into the log. Those two copies are s2 and s6. The treatment words are not a copy.
The design does not post the record to the ERP and does not raise a weather alert.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours cover a broken field map and a new treatment type. The check time for a mismatched reading is already inside s4.
unknowns: Whether this site's station feed supplies station id, reading time, wind speed, air temperature and water temperature.
Which staff roles may read a guest treatment note under national rules.
research_questions: What lawful basis does this operator use to store a guest's treatment note, and who may open it?

already_counted.description: Time in the conditions check when a station reading does not match the beach or slope she saw.

incremental.description: Repair the weather-station field map when a reading name changes, and add a treatment type the form lacks.

approvals.approved_version: confirmed day record she accepted in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A pool day with no station feed, where she types the day once, saves nothing because the sheet fill does not run. A beach day with a live feed and several condition lines she would have copied by hand saves about six percent, and she still writes every treatment and checks every line. Three hours of upkeep are already off the net. No vendor timing figure is used.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still watches the water, beach or slope, decides when an injury needs emergency personnel, and warns guests herself. She no longer copies station readings onto the conditions sheet, and she no longer recopies a confirmed day into the incident log.
reach: A crossing guard keeps the same rule: watching the people who are there stays the whole task, and a conditions log must not take her eyes off them.
skills_to_grow: Spot a station reading that does not match the beach or slope she sees.
Refuse a treatment line that lacks the person, the care or the time.
role.ambitious_version: Every staffed beach and slope closes its conditions and incident record before the post shuts. The call to emergency personnel and the warning to guests stay her decision on every case.
